third_paragraph.2: This directed sampling is a behavioral specialization within one sensory surface. The star provides broad initial coverage while a small region repeatedly inspects potential prey, in the way that an eye scans a scene and then fixates on a target.
third_paragraph.4: The repeated use of ray 11 justifies calling it a tactile fovea. Its behavior resembles target-directed visual fixation, because the sensory surface moves until its most sensitive region meets the target. The star inspects the prey, and the teeth then perform the grasping.
third_paragraph.5: The shortest sequences took 120 ms and spanned foveation, grasping and eating of small prey. Larger earthworm segments took about 19 s to handle, so small prey are processed in a distinct, rapid sequence.
third_paragraph.6: These timings support the proposal that fast sampling sometimes outruns the completed feeding decision, because a contact of about 25 ms is short relative to a cortical onset near 12 ms plus about 5 ms of motor delay.
third_paragraph.7: Rapid handling can therefore make tiny prey valuable even when individual items contain little energy. Profitability divides energy by handling time, so a short handling time raises the return from a small item, while the long handling time of large segments reduces the advantage of their greater energy content.
third_paragraph.8: This comparison links expanded anatomy to a plausible search advantage. Multiplying the area of each touch by the number of touches per second gives the encounter opportunity, and the star's larger area per touch and higher rate both raise it.
third_paragraph.9: The anatomical comparison and behavior support coordinated sensory and feeding specializations. The reduced, tweezer-like incisors sit next to the fovea, so the movement that positions ray 11 also brings the teeth to prey as small as 0.8 mm across.
third_paragraph.10: Each organ is supplied by several endings, and individual fibers may branch, so counting organs measures the distribution of anatomical units across the star. Because every dome has an external structure, receptor-unit density and position can be mapped across all 22 rays.
third_paragraph.11: This organization provides several potential contact-sensitive elements within one dome. A central ending, seven satellite fibers and an outer ring of smaller peripheral endings occupy different positions, so one dome contains structurally distinct endings arranged in concentric rings.
third_paragraph.12: Its position and morphology fit a receptor system for maintained contact. The complex lies near the base of the organ, separate from the superficial central and satellite endings, so one dome contains receptors at two depths. Merkel-like slowly adapting responses were found in the physiological recordings.
third_paragraph.13: The arrangement is consistent with sensitivity to changing mechanical input. Layered capsule tissue surrounds the terminal neurite, and Pacinian-like rapidly adapting responses were recorded from mole nasal afferents. The skin unit integrates several receptor components.
third_paragraph.14: These markers support light-touch and nociceptive specialization. NF200 labels the central and satellite endings while substance P labels the outer ring, so endings that differ in molecular identity sit at different positions within one organ. A nociceptor detects potentially damaging stimulation.
third_paragraph.15: These observations support branching of afferents across the organ's specialized endings. Central and satellite terminals that label together can belong to one fiber, so profiles that look like separate points share an underlying neuronal process.
third_paragraph.16: The branch arrangement provides a tractable way to measure afferent allocation, since the fibers of each ray can be counted separately and related to its organs and cortical stripe. Counting fibers and counting organs give complementary measurements of the sensory periphery.
third_paragraph.17: This association supports richer neural sampling of the foveal organs. The highest afferent number per organ on ray 11 means that each dome there is served by more fibers than elsewhere, while branching, response properties and central allocation also shape how the surface is represented.
third_paragraph.18: The gradient means that contact location changes the density of sampled units even within one ray, with the tips carrying the finest array. Because position along a ray is separate from ray identity, the gradient can be compared across all rays.
third_paragraph.19: The findings reveal a mismatch between dome density and central allocation: ray 11 has typical density but a much larger cortical area per organ. Central magnification is therefore one measured contributor to foveal acuity.
third_paragraph.20: The largest organs, roughly 25 times the area of the smallest, cluster near the star's center, so the footprint of the sensory unit differs between central and distal regions. That variation could change how a contacting object distributes force across sensory units.
third_paragraph.21: These classes provide complementary information about contact presence and contact change. Slowly adapting responses report held contact, while rapidly adapting responses report changes in indentation or a single onset, so the nasal afferent population carries several peripheral codes at once.
third_paragraph.22: The results support parallel channels for distinct mechanical changes. Pacinian-like units prefer small displacements near 250–300 Hz, while other rapidly adapting units respond across broader ranges, so receptor class sets which vibrations drive the afferent.
third_paragraph.23: The findings support sensitivity to the temporal mechanics of natural sampling. A probe speed of 46.2 mm/s matched the measured nose speed during foraging, and some rapidly adapting units followed every stimulus at that speed, so these afferents operate within the speed range of natural touches.
third_paragraph.24: The enrichment supports specialization of the input population supplying the star, in addition to peripheral branching. A TG weighted toward NF200-labeled neurons contains a larger share of large, myelinated touch-associated cell bodies than the body ganglion of the same animal.
third_paragraph.25: The comparison supports a mechanosensitive neuronal population. A 10% radial stretch activated about 80% of TG neurons, so the facial ganglion contains many cells that respond directly to deformation, and the calcium rise reports cellular activation by the stimulus.
third_paragraph.26: The results support a sensory trade-off favoring facial mechanosensitivity over several chemical sensitivities. TG neurons responded more to stretch, hypotonic solution and sanshool but less to capsaicin, so the ganglion supplying the star is weighted toward mechanical detection while a subset still responds to chemical agonists.
third_paragraph.27: This comparison identifies expression patterns that distinguish the facial ganglion from the body ganglion. The mouse comparison separates differences shared across mammals from those specific to the mole, which nominates genes for functional testing.
third_paragraph.28: These results nominate molecules for functional testing. ASIC3, Piezo1, cyclic-nucleotide-gated channels and stomatin-related proteins in the facial ganglion are candidates for converting dome deformation into current, and the TRP and sodium-channel genes enriched in DRG match nociceptive neurons.
third_paragraph.29: Agreement between sequencing and qPCR strengthens the expression claim for Cnga2, Stoml3, Trpa1 and Trpv1. Stomatin-related proteins can modulate channels, which makes Stoml3 a candidate modulator of channels in the facial ganglion.
third_paragraph.30: This provides spatial validation beyond a bulk RNA comparison. The protein localizes to the same touch-associated fibers that carry the NF200 marker, which confirms at the protein level the enrichment seen in RNA.
third_paragraph.31: The approach connects a specialized animal's molecular screen with possible mechanistic experiments, because candidate genes detected in mouse ganglia can be examined with mouse tools. An orthologous gene present in both species is the starting point for testing function.
third_paragraph.32: The enlargement marks a major specialization before signals reach cortex. Cytochrome-oxidase subdivisions inside PrV were compared with receptive-field mapping to determine which rays the visible subdivisions represent.
third_paragraph.33: The histological pattern supports a topographic organization, and electrophysiology tested the assignments. Because the 11 modules correspond to the 11 rays and the module of ray 11 is large, the outlines form a brainstem map of the nose, confirmed by responses to controlled stimulation.
third_paragraph.34: The results establish ray-related activity within PrV. Lesion marks aligned with stained sections link each recorded response to its module, so a neuron that responds to a given ray lies in the module assigned to that ray.
third_paragraph.35: The comparison indicates that magnification builds up in steps, with the foveal ray receiving a larger share of neural tissue at each successive stage. Allocation is therefore a distributional transformation and not a uniform scaling of the periphery.
third_paragraph.36: The visible stripes allow anatomical area to be compared with measured peripheral innervation. Two stripe sets, one for S1 and one for S2, each hold a separate map of the opposite side of the nose, and the enlarged foveal territory is visible in S1.
third_paragraph.37: The result establishes unequal central investment per counted input. Ray 11 keeps the largest cortical allocation after normalization by afferent number, which is consistent with functional specialization associated with its preferential behavioral use.
third_paragraph.38: The smaller foveal fields support finer spatial sampling in the disproportionately large representation. A smaller field means that a touch at a given location drives a more restricted group of cortical neurons, with 0.59 mm² on ray 11 against 0.82 mm² on rays 1–10.
third_paragraph.39: The common onset latency of 11.6 ms for 5-ms and 500-ms stimuli supports fast transmission that is not determined by total contact duration. The latency fits the cortical tactile onset near 12 ms used in the double-take timing.
third_paragraph.40: The timing supports a code sensitive to transitions as well as continuing contact. About 61% of neurons carried an OFF response at 12.2 ms, so release of the stimulus is signaled about as quickly as its onset.
third_paragraph.41: The findings support interactions that sharpen the spatial pattern of cortical activity. One contact raises activity at its own location and lowers it at neighboring ones, which increases the contrast between them.
third_paragraph.42: The positional dependence supports a spatially structured response in which excitation at the center and suppression in the surround define a response boundary within a ray.
third_paragraph.43: The comparison supports multiple temporal representations of contact duration within cortex. A short natural touch can activate these neurons without reproducing their response to a long hold, so duration is coded by which neurons stay active.
third_paragraph.44: This developmental sequence establishes how the star's basic structure emerges. Rays arise from epidermal crests that form between embryo lengths of 9 and 15 mm, and embryo length serves as a staging measure for these steps.
third_paragraph.45: The sequence supports coordinated development of the receptor surface and its innervation. Nerve organization into fascicles and ring-like terminal arrangements are in place before rays emerge about one week after birth, so anatomical specialization precedes free ray movement.

inserts.title: Frame rate sets the timing resolution of video
paragraphs: Frame rate is the number of images that a camera records each second, and it sets the shortest event that a video record can resolve. A fast camera divides a brief movement into many successive images, whereas a slow camera collapses it into one or two.

Catania and Remple filmed feeding through a glass-bottom tunnel at 500 frames per second. Earthworm fragments supplied prey, and the transparent floor preserved a clear view of the star. Search movements lasted about 50 ms and touches about 25 ms, giving approximately 13 contacts per second.

The earlier work of Catania and Kaas used 30 frames per second, so those frame numbers identify successive observations. The 500 frames per second recording resolves individual touches and the movements between them, which allows contact time and search time to be measured separately.
notes: Timing measurements from video depend on how many images the camera records each second.
Definition.
Frame rate is the number of images recorded per second.
It sets the shortest event that a video can resolve.
Fast and slow cameras.
A fast camera divides a brief movement into many successive images.
A slow camera collapses the same movement into one or two images.
Setup.
Catania and Remple filmed feeding through a glass-bottom tunnel.
The transparent floor preserved a clear view of the star.
Prey.
Earthworm fragments supplied the prey that the moles sampled and ate.
Timing result.
Search movements lasted about 50 milliseconds and touches about 25 milliseconds.
The sampling rate was approximately 13 contacts per second.
Comparison with earlier work.
The recordings of Catania and Kaas used 30 frames per second.
Their frame numbers identify successive observations and do not give millisecond-precise events.
Meaning.
A recording at 500 frames per second resolves individual touches and the movements between them.
Starting point.
The earlier records are valuable for the sequence of contacts, which identifies which ray touched the prey first.
Ray 11 is the final position that the prey reaches.
Meaning for the study.
Both recordings answer different questions, one about order and one about duration.

inserts.title: Latency is the delay between stimulus and response
paragraphs: Latency is the time from a stimulus until a response begins. Sensory latency is the delay before neurons change their firing, and motor delay is the time for a command to reach the muscles. Each stage adds to the total time between a touch and a reaction.

In the double-take analysis, a typical contact lasted about 25 ms. Prior cortical recordings placed tactile response onset near 12 ms, and Catania and Remple estimated about 5 ms for a motor command to reach the periphery. Double takes occurred in more than one-third of their feeding trials.

Latencies of this size are comparable to the 25 ms of a single touch. When the star leaves a contact before the decision to eat is complete, it reverses and returns, which produces the double take. The proposal is that fast sampling sometimes outruns the completed feeding decision.
notes: Several delays separate a touch from the movement that follows it.
Definition.
Latency is the time from a stimulus until a response begins.
Each processing stage adds its own delay.
Sensory and motor stages.
Sensory latency is the delay before neurons change their firing.
Motor delay is the time for a command to reach the muscles.
Contact duration.
A typical contact lasted about 25 milliseconds.
Neural timing.
Prior cortical recordings placed tactile response onset near 12 milliseconds.
Catania and Remple estimated about 5 milliseconds for a motor command to reach the periphery.
Double takes.
The star moves away from a contacted item, then reverses and places the fovea onto it.
These sequences occurred in more than one-third of feeding trials.
Proposal.
Fast sampling sometimes outruns the completed feeding decision.
The star leaves the contact before the decision to eat is finished.
Why timing matters.
The star touches about 13 times each second, so each decision must be made within a few tens of milliseconds.
A reversal appears in video as the star moving away and then back onto the prey.
Sources of the numbers.
The cortical onset came from prior recordings, and the motor figure was an estimate by the authors.

inserts.title: Scanning electron microscopy images fine surface structure
paragraphs: Scanning electron microscopy images the surface of a specimen by scanning it with a focused beam of electrons. The method resolves fine surface structure, such as the shape and spacing of small domes, at much higher magnification than a light microscope.

Sawyer and Catania used it to map Eimer's organs across the flattened front surface of the star. The star contains roughly 25,000 organs across its 22 rays, and surface images reveal separate domes packed into a repeated array.

Each dome has an external structure, so organ position can be measured directly from the image without tracing its innervation. The same images supply organ density, position along each ray and the frontal area of individual organs.
notes: Surface imaging made it possible to count and map sensory units across the whole star.
Method.
Scanning electron microscopy scans a specimen with a focused beam of electrons.
It resolves fine surface structure at high magnification.
Specimen.
Sawyer and Catania imaged the flattened front surface of the star.
Eimer's organs.
The star contains roughly 25,000 organs across its 22 rays.
Surface images reveal separate domes packed into a repeated array.
Direct measurement.
Each unit has an external structure that can be identified.
Its position can be read from the image without tracing its entire innervation.
Other measures from the same images.
Density of organs, eccentricity along each ray and the frontal surface area of individual organs all come from the micrographs.
Comparison with other mammals.
Many mammalian touch receptors have no externally visible unit, so the star offers an unusually accessible array.
Why a flattened star.
Flattening the star places all of its surface in one plane so that the domes can be imaged and counted together.
Organ structure.
An Eimer's organ is a small epidermal sensory unit containing several types of nerve ending.
The epidermis is the outer cellular layer of skin.

inserts.title: Confocal microscopy resolves endings at a chosen depth
paragraphs: Confocal microscopy forms an image from a single thin optical plane of a fluorescently labeled specimen, rejecting light from above and below that plane. Stacking planes at different depths reconstructs the three-dimensional arrangement of labeled structures.

Marasco and colleagues used fluorescent dyes and confocal microscopy to examine Eimer's organs in horizontal and vertical sections. About 15 µm below the apex, a central ending was surrounded by seven satellite fibers, and a second, outer ring contained smaller peripheral endings.

Optical sectioning places each ending at a defined depth and ring position. Near the surface, terminal swellings of the satellite fibers approach the central terminal, an arrangement that a surface image alone could not reveal.
inserts.citation: Marasco et al. (2006); Gerhold et al. (2013)
notes: Optical sectioning allows the internal arrangement of an organ to be read from fluorescent labels.
Method.
Confocal microscopy images a single thin plane of a fluorescent specimen.
Light from above and below the plane is rejected.
Stacks.
Images from different depths reconstruct the three-dimensional arrangement of labeled structures.
Sections.
Marasco and colleagues examined horizontal and vertical tissue sections.
The arrangement of nerve terminals was compared across sections and not inferred from the surface.
Central ending.
About 15 micrometers below the apex a central ending was surrounded by seven satellite fibers in the illustrated specimen.
Outer ring.
A second ring contained smaller peripheral endings.
Near the surface.
Terminal swellings of the satellite fibers approached the central terminal.
Why dyes.
Fluorescent dyes label nerve terminals, so their positions can be compared across sections.
Different colors mark different structures in the same specimen.
Horizontal and vertical sections.
Sections cut in two orientations show the rings from above and the layers from the side.

inserts.title: Double labeling marks two molecules in one section
paragraphs: Double labeling uses two antibodies with different fluorescent colors to mark two molecules in the same tissue section. Because both labels appear in one structure, the positions of the two populations can be compared directly.

Marasco and colleagues double-labeled coast mole Eimer's organs for NF200 and substance P. Central and satellite endings labeled for NF200, whereas the outer peripheral ring labeled for substance P. Gerhold and colleagues found strong NF200 staining and sparse peripheral substance-P staining in star-nosed mole organs.

NF200 marks many large, myelinated sensory fibers, and substance P marks a subset of pain-signaling neurons. Each ending can therefore be assigned to a molecular class by its position within the organ.
inserts.citation: Marasco et al. (2006); Gerhold et al. (2013)
notes: Two molecular markers in one section separate neighboring endings by identity.
Method.
Double labeling uses two antibodies with different fluorescent colors.
Both labels appear in the same tissue section.
NF200 is a neurofilament marker associated with many large, myelinated sensory fibers.
Substance P.
Substance P is a neuropeptide associated with a subset of pain-signaling neurons.
Coast mole result.
Central and satellite endings labeled for NF200.
The outer peripheral ring labeled for substance P.
Star-nosed mole result.
Gerhold and colleagues found strong NF200 staining and sparse peripheral substance-P staining.
Meaning.
Position within the organ corresponds to molecular class, so the peripheral ring is not an undifferentiated set of endings.
Why two species.
The coast mole organs were double-labeled by Marasco and colleagues.
Gerhold and colleagues examined the star-nosed mole organs afterward.
Terminal position.
The two studies distinguish terminal position from a single undifferentiated ring.

inserts.title: Adaptation separates held contact from changing contact
paragraphs: Adaptation is a decline in a sensory neuron's firing during a continued stimulus. A slowly adapting afferent keeps firing throughout a maintained indentation and reports that contact is present, whereas a rapidly adapting afferent fires mainly when the indentation changes.

Marasco and Catania recorded single units from the trigeminal ganglion while controlled stimulators contacted the nose for 500 ms. Some receptors fired throughout the static portion, producing slowly adapting, Merkel-like responses. Others responded to changing indentation, and one rapidly adapting response produced a single onset impulse.

The classes carry complementary information: presence of contact from slowly adapting units and change of contact from rapidly adapting units. A single nose therefore sends several peripheral codes to the brain for the same touch.
notes: Different afferents respond differently to the same maintained indentation.
Definition.
Adaptation is a change in firing during continued stimulation.
The firing rate declines at a rate that depends on the receptor.
Slowly adapting.
These afferents fire throughout the static portion of the indentation.
They report that contact is present.
Rapidly adapting.
These afferents respond mainly to changing indentation.
One class produced a single onset impulse.
Recordings.
Marasco and Catania recorded single units from the trigeminal ganglion.
Controlled stimulators contacted the nose for 500 milliseconds.
Merkel-like responses.
Slowly adapting responses resembled those of Merkel cell receptors.
Meaning.
Contact presence and contact change are carried by different afferent classes, so one touch generates several parallel signals.
Stimulus.
A controlled stimulator indented the nose in a stationary hold of 500 milliseconds.
This is different from freely chosen touches.
Response types.
Merkel-like units fired throughout the hold.
Rapidly adapting units fired when the indentation changed.

inserts.title: Fura-2 reports calcium in cultured neurons
paragraphs: Fura-2 is a fluorescent calcium indicator whose emission changes when it binds calcium. Because calcium enters neurons when they are activated, a rise in the indicator signal reports activation of an individual cultured cell. Cultured cells can be compared under one mechanical protocol.

Gerhold and colleagues isolated TG and DRG neurons and cultured them on deformable substrates. A 10% radial stretch was applied under a shared protocol, and about 80% of TG neurons responded, compared with 34% of DRG neurons. Both tissues were exposed to the same stretch, so the difference in responses belongs to the neurons.

The original images retain the authors' calcium-response colors, so responding cells appear as a change in color. The higher fraction of responding TG neurons agrees with the greater fraction of touch-associated markers in the facial ganglion.
notes: A fluorescent calcium indicator allows cultured neurons to report their response to deformation.
Indicator.
Fura-2 is a fluorescent calcium indicator.
Its signal changes when it binds calcium.
Why calcium.
Calcium enters neurons when they are activated.
A rise in the signal reports cellular activation.
Culture.
Gerhold and colleagues isolated TG and DRG neurons.
The neurons were cultured on deformable substrates.
Stimulus.
A 10 percent radial stretch was applied to both tissues under a shared protocol.
Result.
About 80 percent of TG neurons responded.
In DRG neurons the figure was 34 percent.
Agreement with markers.
The enrichment of responses in TG matches its greater fraction of touch-associated markers.
Tissue comparison.
TG neurons come from the ganglion serving the face and DRG neurons from the one serving the body.
Both were cultured and stretched in the same way.
Colors.
The images retain the authors' calcium-response colors, so a responding cell changes color when calcium rises.

inserts.title: A transcriptome is the set of RNAs a tissue expresses
paragraphs: A transcriptome is the full collection of RNA transcripts expressed in a tissue. RNA sequencing reads these transcripts and counts them, so genes with more transcripts are inferred to be expressed more strongly in that tissue.

Gerhold and colleagues sequenced TG and DRG of star-nosed moles. Without an annotated genome, reads were aligned successively against human, dog and mouse transcript sequences, assigning approximately 42–65% of reads. Thousands of genes differed between the two ganglia.

A parallel mouse TG–DRG comparison separates differences shared across mammals from those potentially associated with the mole's specialized facial sensory population. Genes that differ only in the mole become candidates for the specialization of the star.
notes: Sequencing the RNA of a tissue lists the genes that it is actively using.
Definition.
A transcriptome is the collection of RNA transcripts in a tissue.
RNA sequencing reads and counts these transcripts.
Tissues.
Gerhold and colleagues compared the trigeminal ganglion with the dorsal root ganglia of star-nosed moles.
The first serves the face and the second serves the body.
No annotated genome.
Reads were aligned successively against human, dog and mouse transcript sequences.
Coverage.
The approach assigned approximately 42 to 65 percent of sequenced reads.
Thousands of genes differed between the two mole ganglia.
Mouse comparison.
A parallel mouse comparison separated differences shared across mammals from those associated with the mole.
Meaning.
Expression differences nominate genes for functional testing.
Why three genomes.
The star-nosed mole genome was not annotated, so human, dog and mouse sequences served as references in turn.
Bulk tissue.
The sequencing samples whole ganglia, which contain neurons and supporting cells.

inserts.title: Quantitative PCR checks selected genes independently
paragraphs: Quantitative PCR, or qPCR, measures the amount of a selected RNA target by amplifying it and monitoring the product during amplification. Expression of each target is normalized to a reference transcript so that samples can be compared.

Gerhold and colleagues tested several TG- and DRG-enriched candidates. Cnga2 and Stoml3 were more highly expressed in TG, whereas Trpa1 and Trpv1 were more highly expressed in DRG. Fam38a, the Piezo1 gene, followed the TG-directed trend, but its difference was not established convincingly.

Agreement with the sequencing screen strengthens an expression claim, because a second method measures the same genes independently. The assay retains most candidates for further testing and marks Piezo1 as less certain than the others.
notes: A second method on selected genes tests whether the sequencing screen was reliable.
Method.
Quantitative PCR amplifies a selected RNA target.
The product is monitored during amplification.
Normalization.
Expression is normalized to a reference transcript.
This allows samples to be compared.
TG-enriched genes.
Cnga2 and Stoml3 were more highly expressed in the trigeminal ganglion.
DRG-enriched genes.
Trpa1 and Trpv1 were more highly expressed in the dorsal root ganglia.
Piezo1.
Fam38a, the Piezo1 gene, followed the TG-directed trend.
Its difference in this assay was not established convincingly.
Meaning.
Agreement across independent assays strengthens an expression claim, and function remains to be tested.
Reference transcript.
A reference transcript corrects for differences in the amount of starting material.
Each candidate is then expressed relative to it.
Candidates.
Cnga2 and Stoml3 favored the face-serving ganglion.
Trpa1 and Trpv1 favored the body-serving ganglion.

inserts.title: Cytochrome oxidase staining reveals active regions
paragraphs: Cytochrome oxidase is a mitochondrial enzyme, and tissue stained for it appears darker where neurons are metabolically more active. In brain sections the stain reveals boundaries between regions that differ in their activity. The staining is applied to tissue sections after the brain has been removed.

Catania, Leitch and Gauthier stained brainstem sections from star-nosed and hairy-tailed moles. In the star-nosed mole, PrV was greatly expanded and bulged toward the incoming trigeminal nerve, and cytochrome-oxidase staining revealed strong internal subdivisions.

The adjacent spinal trigeminal complex provided an anatomical comparison. The same staining approach, applied to flattened cortex, reveals the stripes of the cortical star, so one histological marker links brainstem and cortex. The comparison with the hairy-tailed mole relates central anatomy to a different nasal receptor surface.
notes: A metabolic stain makes the internal organization of the brainstem visible.
Stain.
Cytochrome oxidase is a mitochondrial enzyme.
Tissue stains darker where neurons are metabolically more active.
Sections.
Catania, Leitch and Gauthier stained brainstem sections.
They compared star-nosed and hairy-tailed moles.
Star-nosed mole PrV.
PrV was greatly expanded and bulged toward the incoming trigeminal nerve.
Subdivisions.
The stain revealed strong internal subdivisions.
Comparison region.
The adjacent spinal trigeminal complex provided an anatomical comparison.
It was not evidence that all facial nuclei expanded equally.
Cortex.
The same stain applied to flattened cortex reveals the stripes of the cortical star.
Species comparison.
The hairy-tailed mole, Parascalops breweri, has a different nasal receptor surface.
Comparing the two relates central anatomy to peripheral specialization.
PrV.
The principal trigeminal nucleus is a brainstem relay for facial mechanosensory input.

inserts.title: A receptive field is the territory a neuron responds to
paragraphs: A receptive field is the region of the sensory surface whose stimulation changes the activity of a recorded neuron. Mapping fields while recording turns an anatomical module into a functional territory on the skin. The pairing of stimulus and recording site gives each module a functional label.

Catania and colleagues recorded neural responses while gently stimulating identified nasal rays. They marked selected electrode locations with small lesions and aligned these marks with stained sections. Responses encountered along penetrations changed according to the module entered. The stimuli were gentle contacts applied to individual rays.

Pairing the stimulation territory with the recording location is stronger evidence than labeling modules from resemblance alone. Each module of the 11-module PrV pattern can be assigned to a ray from the receptive fields recorded in it.
notes: Recording from a module and finding where on the nose it responds links anatomy to function.
Definition.
A receptive field is the peripheral region whose stimulation changes a recorded neuron's activity.
Stimulation.
Catania and colleagues gently stimulated identified nasal rays while recording.
Lesion marks.
Selected electrode locations were marked with small lesions.
The marks were aligned with stained sections.
Responses.
Responses along penetrations changed according to the module entered.
Assignments.
Lesion positions and serial sections related functional assignments to the 11-module pattern.
Evidence.
The paired record of stimulation territory and recording location is stronger than labeling modules from resemblance alone.
Penetrations.
Each electrode track passed through several modules.
Responses changed as the electrode entered each new module.
Controls on location.
Some penetrations also encountered trigeminal-nerve or spinal-nucleus responses, so location was checked in the stained sections.

inserts.title: Tangential sections expose the layout of cortex
paragraphs: A tangential section is a slice cut parallel to the cortical surface, and flattening the cortex before cutting places the whole sheet in one plane. Such sections reveal how an area is laid out across the surface, unlike slices cut perpendicular to it.

Catania and Kaas flattened cortex and cut tangential sections, then processed them for cytochrome oxidase. Two pinwheel-like sets of stripes appeared, corresponding to S1 and S2 star representations. Electrophysiological mapping associated stripes with input from rays on the opposite side of the nose.
The foveal ray occupied an especially large S1 territory. The stripes allow cortical area to be measured for each ray and compared with the myelinated-fiber counts of the same ray.
notes: The plane of a tissue section determines which spatial relationships can be seen.
Definition.
A tangential section is cut parallel to the cortical surface.
Flattening the cortex first places the whole sheet in one plane.
Why flatten.
The layout of an area across the surface becomes visible.
Slices cut perpendicular to the surface show only a narrow strip.
Staining.
Catania and Kaas processed the sections for cytochrome oxidase.
Result.
Two pinwheel-like sets of stripes appeared.
They corresponded to S1 and S2 star representations.
Mapping.
Electrophysiological mapping associated stripes with input from rays on the opposite side of the nose.
Fovea.
The foveal ray occupied an especially large S1 territory.
S1 and S2.
S1 is primary somatosensory cortex and S2 is a secondary processing area with its own map.
Pinwheel arrangement.
The stripes are arranged around a center like the rays of the nose.
Each set represents the opposite side of the nose.

inserts.title: Multiunit activity maps where skin drives cortex
paragraphs: Multiunit activity is the combined spiking of several neurons near an electrode, recorded without separating individual cells. It is a robust signal for mapping where on the skin stimulation drives a local group of neurons.

Sachdev and Catania mapped excitatory receptive fields in anesthetized moles. A fine glass probe contacted individual parts of the star under a microscope. Mean excitatory field area was 0.59 mm² on ray 11 and 0.82 mm² on rays 1–10.

Boundaries were sharply defined by the fall in evoked activity outside each field, and most fields occupied a continuous patch within one ray. A multiunit field is the area over which a small group of neurons responds, which differs from the field of a single isolated neuron.
notes: Recording a small group of neurons at once gives a stable map of the skin territory they serve.
Definition.
Multiunit activity combines spikes from nearby neurons.
Individual cells are not separated.
Mapping.
A fine glass probe contacted individual parts of the star under a microscope.
The recordings came from anesthetized moles.
Field size.
Mean excitatory field area was 0.59 square millimeters on ray 11.
It was 0.82 square millimeters on rays 1 to 10.
Boundaries.
Field edges were sharply defined by the fall in evoked activity outside each field.
Location.
Most fields occupied a continuous patch within one ray and did not span the whole star.
Meaning.
A multiunit field differs from the field of a single isolated neuron.
Recording preparation.
The moles were anesthetized during mapping.
Cortical activity was recorded while the probe touched the star.
Comparison of rays.
Ray 11 had smaller fields than rays 1 to 10.
Its representation in cortex is also disproportionately large.

inserts.title: Center–surround organization sharpens the cortical map
paragraphs: Center–surround organization means that stimulation of a central receptive region excites a neuron, whereas stimulation of the region around it reduces the neuron's activity. The reduction is measured relative to spontaneous firing. Both center and surround are defined for a single neuron.

Sachdev and Catania recorded simultaneously at electrodes separated by 200 µm while moving a probe among mapped sites. In paired examples, one contact excited a neuron whose field included that position and suppressed another whose field lay elsewhere.

Suppression separates an inhibitory influence from simply failing to excite a neuron at an unrelated location. Most inhibitory surrounds were larger than the central excitatory patch, yet remained largely confined to one ray. The paired recordings came from separate neurons whose fields lay at different positions.
notes: A touch excites some cortical neurons and suppresses their neighbors.
Definition.
Center–surround organization pairs excitation in the center of a field with reduced activity in the surround.
Reference level.
Suppression is measured relative to spontaneous firing.
Recordings.
Sachdev and Catania recorded at electrodes separated by 200 micrometers.
They moved the probe among mapped sites.
Paired example.
One contact excited a neuron whose field included that position.
The same contact suppressed another neuron whose field lay elsewhere.
Inhibition.
Suppression is different from merely failing to excite a neuron.
Extent.
Most inhibitory surrounds were larger than the excitatory patch.
They remained largely confined to one ray.
Electrode spacing.
Two electrodes 200 micrometers apart recorded neurons with different fields at the same time.
Baseline.
Spontaneous firing provides the reference for a decrease.
A neuron that simply does not respond stays at baseline.
